title: Slow-Cooked Massaman Beef Curry with Potatoes and Peanuts
summary: A rich Thai-style massaman beef curry with tender slow-cooked beef, soft potatoes and crunchy peanuts in a fragrant coconut sauce. It is warming, gently spiced and ideal for a comforting dairy-free dinner.

ingredients.name: beef stewing steak, cut into large chunks
potatoes, peeled and cut into 4 cm chunks

steps: Pat the beef dry and season it with the salt. Heat the vegetable oil in a large heavy casserole over medium-high heat, then brown the beef in batches for 3–4 minutes per batch until deeply coloured on the outside. Transfer the beef to a plate.
Lower the heat to medium. Add the sliced onion to the same pan and cook for 5 minutes, stirring often, until softened and lightly golden.
Add the garlic, ginger and chilli and cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Stir in the curry powder, cumin, ground coriander, cinnamon and cardamom, and cook for 30 seconds to toast the spices.

Pour in a little of the coconut milk and scrape the base of the pan to loosen any browned bits. Add the remaining coconut milk, coconut cream, vegetable stock, tamari, brown sugar, lime juice and bay leaf, then stir well.

Return the beef and any resting juices to the pan. Bring to a gentle simmer, cover with a lid and cook over very low heat for 2 hours, stirring occasionally, until the beef is starting to become tender.
Add the potato chunks and 50 g of the peanuts. Cover again and simmer gently for 35–45 minutes, until the potatoes are soft and the beef pulls apart easily with a fork.
Remove the bay leaf. Simmer uncovered for 5–10 minutes if the sauce needs thickening, then taste and adjust with a little more salt or lime juice if needed.
Serve hot, scattered with the remaining peanuts and chopped fresh coriander.
